quizzes.title: Devolution and the Asymmetric UK Framework
quizzes.passage:
Devolution refers to the transfer of powers from a central government to subnational institutions. The central government does not give up everything in this process, because it keeps ultimate constitutional authority. In the United Kingdom, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland have devolved institutions. However, the extent and nature of the powers given to each differ, so the framework is asymmetric rather than uniform. The present arrangements have taken shape over a long constitutional history, and debate about them has grown in recent years. Different parts of the country have also reached different views on several of these questions.

Money is a central part of the relationship between Westminster and the devolved administrations. Changes in block grant funding for these bodies are set using a formula. Questions about how resources are allocated have become part of wider debates on the country's fiscal and constitutional arrangements. Legal rules matter too. After the United Kingdom left the European Union, a law was passed to regulate the domestic market within the country. Its effect on the powers of devolved governments has been a subject of argument, and it has become one more point of tension in the debate. Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland have each had their own institutions since the late 1990s. The framework therefore links constitutional questions with questions about money and law.

questions.q: The Government of Wales Act 1998 established which body?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the Government of Wales Act 1998 established the Welsh Legislature.

questions.q: The Welsh Legislature is now known by which name?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Welsh Legislature is now known as the Senedd.

questions.q: In which year was the UK Internal Market Act passed?
questions.explanation: The booklet dates the UK Internal Market Act to 2020.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Devolved governments criticised the UK Internal Market Act, 2020.
Reason (R): The Act regulates the domestic UK market after Brexit.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are in the booklet, but the criticism was about reduced regulatory autonomy, not about the Act's purpose.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. UK Internal Market Act, 2020   ->   A. Regulates the domestic UK market after Brexit
II. Barnett Formula   ->   B. Sets changes in block grant funding
III. Devolution   ->   C. Transfer of powers to subnational institutions
IV. Asymmetric devolution   ->   D. Devolved powers differ in extent and nature
questions.explanation: Each item matches the description the booklet gives for it.

questions.q:
Statements about UK devolution:
I. The Government of Wales Act 1998 established the Welsh Legislature.
II. Devolved governments welcomed the UK Internal Market Act, 2020 as increasing their autonomy.
III. Changes in block grant funding are set by the Scottish Parliament.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement I is in the booklet, while II and III contradict it: the Act was criticised, and the Barnett Formula is used by the UK Treasury.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about UK devolution are correct?
I. The Barnett Formula is used to set changes in block grant funding.
II. Devolved powers are identical in all three devolved territories.
III. Devolved governments criticised the UK Internal Market Act, 2020.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while II is wrong because the booklet says the powers differ.

quizzes.title: Devolution and the Asymmetric UK Framework
quizzes.passage:
Devolution is a feature of the constitutional arrangements of the United Kingdom. Under it, powers move from the central government to institutions below the national level, yet the centre continues to hold ultimate constitutional authority. Three territories of the UK have such institutions: Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland. Their powers are not identical, because the extent and nature of what each can do differ. For this reason the framework is often described as asymmetric.

Wales has its own legislature, which was created by a law passed in 1998. Scotland's parliament was created by another law of the same year. Money is also part of the picture. The sums given to devolved administrations change according to a formula applied by one central department. Questions about how resources are allocated therefore form part of wider debates on the country's fiscal and constitutional arrangements.

Recently, a law was passed to regulate the domestic market across the UK after the country left the European Union. Its effects on devolved governments have been debated. These are matters that continue to be discussed across the UK. The relationship between Westminster and the devolved administrations is central to this discussion. Different parts of the country have reached different views on these questions.

questions.q: The Welsh legislature created under a 1998 Act of Parliament is now known as what? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Welsh legislature, established in 1998, is now known as the Senedd.

questions.q: Which 1998 Act of Parliament established the Welsh legislature? (name of the Act)
questions.explanation: The booklet names the Government of Wales Act 1998 as the law that established the Welsh legislature.

questions.q: Which formula does the UK Treasury use to set changes in block grant funding for devolved administrations? (name of the formula)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Barnett Formula is used by the UK Treasury to determine changes in block grant funding.

questions.q: Devolved governments criticised the UK Internal Market Act, 2020 for reducing their ___ autonomy. (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says devolved governments criticised the 2020 Act as reducing their regulatory autonomy.

questions.q: In which year was the UK Internal Market Act passed? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet dates the UK Internal Market Act to 2020.

questions.q: Which UK body uses the Barnett Formula to set changes in block grant funding? (name of the body)
questions.explanation: The booklet identifies the UK Treasury as the body that uses the Barnett Formula.

questions.q: UK devolution is described as asymmetric rather than what? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says UK devolution is asymmetric rather than uniform.

quizzes.title: Good Friday Agreement and Northern Ireland
quizzes.passage:
The Good Friday, or Belfast, Agreement was a landmark accord for Northern Ireland. It was reached to bring an end to a long period of violence that had divided its people for decades. The agreement set up a system of government in which power would be shared, rather than held by one side alone. It also addressed questions of identity, and it sought to make the border between Northern Ireland and the Republic far less visible. Freedom of movement across the islands was encouraged as part of the settlement. The region's politics has been shaped by the division between those who wish to remain in the UK and those who want a united Ireland.

Its effects have been tested since. When the United Kingdom left the European Union, Northern Ireland found itself with a land border with an EU member state. Checks were then placed between Great Britain and Northern Ireland, and this became a matter of dispute in the region. Political deadlock followed the 2022 election, when a government could not be formed for a time. The UK Government later published a new arrangement to address the problems that had emerged. The Good Friday Agreement remains the reference point for these questions. A border poll is one of the mechanisms the agreement provides for future constitutional change.

questions.q: Under the agreement, who can call a border poll on Irish reunification when conditions show majority support?
options: The UK Secretary of State for Northern Ireland
questions.explanation: The booklet says the UK Secretary of State for Northern Ireland can call a border poll when required conditions show majority support.

questions.q: Under the agreement, people born in Northern Ireland may hold which nationality?
questions.explanation: The booklet says people born in Northern Ireland can hold Irish or British citizenship or both.

questions.q: Under the agreement, the Northern Ireland government would be formed on the wishes of whom?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the government would be formed on the wishes of both Republicans and Unionists, who would share governance equally.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The DUP leader refused to allow government formation after the May 2022 polls in Northern Ireland.
Reason (R): Unionists were angered by border checks between Great Britain and Northern Ireland.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet links the DUP leader's refusal to the Unionist anger over checks between Great Britain and Northern Ireland.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. The Troubles   ->   A. Conflict ended by the Good Friday Agreement
II. Safeguarding the Union   ->   B. Command paper setting out a new deal after the 2022 deadlock
III. Border poll   ->   C. Can be called by the UK Secretary of State for Northern Ireland
IV. Irish or British nationality   ->   D. Citizens may hold either or both
questions.explanation: Each item matches the description the booklet gives for it.

questions.q:
Statements about the Good Friday Agreement:
I. Reunification with Ireland can be sought only through a vote in the UK Parliament, not a referendum.
II. Northern Ireland's government is formed on the wishes of both Republicans and Unionists.
III. Safeguarding the Union was passed as an Act of the Irish parliament.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement II matches the booklet, since reunification is subject to a referendum and Safeguarding the Union is a UK command paper.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about Northern Ireland's arrangements are correct?
I. The agreement abolished border checks across the UK and Ireland.
II. Border checks between Great Britain and Northern Ireland were introduced after Brexit.
III. The DUP leader supported government formation after the May 2022 polls.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are in the booklet, while III is contrary to the refusal described in it.

quizzes.title: Good Friday Agreement and Northern Ireland
quizzes.passage:
The Good Friday Agreement, reached in 1998, was an attempt to bring an end to decades of violence in Northern Ireland. Its main purpose was to create a government in which people with differing views on the region's future would share power. It set out a route by which the region's status could be reconsidered over time, and it recognised the right of people to identify with different national traditions. Freedom of movement across the islands was encouraged, and checks along the border were abolished.

Decades later, the picture changed. When the United Kingdom left the European Union, Northern Ireland came to share a land border with a neighbouring state that belonged to the EU. Checks were then introduced on trade between Great Britain and Northern Ireland. Several parties in the region opposed these checks, arguing that they weakened Northern Ireland's place within the UK.

Political deadlock followed the 2022 election, when a government could not be formed for a time. A new deal was later set out by the UK Government to address these problems. The arrangements since then have raised questions about the region's constitutional status. Power-sharing and border arrangements remain central to the region's politics. The agreement's provisions still shape these discussions.

questions.q: The Good Friday Agreement ended a conflict in Northern Ireland known by what name? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet calls the 30-year conflict that the agreement ended The Troubles.

questions.q: Which party's leader refused to allow government formation after the May 2022 polls in Northern Ireland? (party name; short form accepted)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the leader of the Democratic Unionist Party refused to allow government formation after the May 2022 polls.

questions.q: What is the name of the command paper in which the UK Government published a new deal for Northern Ireland?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the new deal was published as a command paper called Safeguarding the Union.

questions.q: Under the agreement, which office holder can call a border poll on Irish reunification? (office title)
questions.answer: UK Secretary of State for Northern Ireland
accept: Secretary of State for Northern Ireland
questions.explanation: The booklet says the UK Secretary of State for Northern Ireland can call a border poll.

questions.q: Which EU member state shares a land border with Northern Ireland? (name of the state)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Northern Ireland shares a land border with the Republic of Ireland, an EU member.

questions.q: The Good Friday Agreement was signed in which city? (city name)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the agreement was signed at Belfast.

questions.q: Under the agreement, reunification with Ireland may be sought at any time, subject to what? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says people can seek reunification with Ireland at any time, subject to a referendum.
